kind: REN-04 shared domain contract registry (SOURCE OF TRUTH)
readme: This file is the single source from which the tool manifest, input schemas, RPC map, docs and the legacy migration adapter are GENERATED. Nothing downstream may be hand-edited: harness/contract-generator.mjs emits artifacts/generated/* and harness/contract-consistency.mjs fails the build when any consumer disagrees with this registry.

candidate.legacy_tool_count_evidence: evidence/tool-inventory.json reports 69 extracted registrations and an identical name set to openclaw.plugin.json contracts.tools (69)

conventions.clustering: operations are clustered by resource domain, then by risk, then by typical-task adjacency; the resident set is the measured typical production chain, not a raw frequency cut
conventions.no_universal_json_tool_note: every operation has a closed, typed input; no operation accepts an arbitrary JSON payload or a free-form object bag as its work unit
conventions.no_top_level_anyof_oneof_note: variants are expressed as closed enums that select among FLAT typed fields plus explicit mutual-exclusion groups; no top-level anyOf/oneOf appears in any generated schema (the host flattens those, which loses the constraint). Validated by contract-consistency.mjs.
conventions.no_optional_true_marker_note: capability is never hidden behind an optional:true marker; a field is either required, or optional-and-documented, and every enum member is reachable
conventions.required_semantics: every entry in `required` cites the service-layer assertion that enforces it (file:line), so 'required' is a verified claim rather than a copy of the old empty arrays
conventions.legacy_alias_policy: legacy names remain callable through the migration adapter, but they are NOT re-injected as resident tools; the adapter resolves them onto the new operations. Sunset requires call telemetry proving zero use (see sunset_gate).
conventions.single_submit_rule: plan and execute are the SAME operation selected by `mode`; there is no separate plan tool to alias onto a generate tool, so one submission cannot be counted twice by alias or retry. Validated by the alias double-submit case in the regression guardrails.

budget.resident_max_basis: parent design budget; REN-04 is exactly at it (10 resident operations)
budget.surface_metric: REN-03 ab_metric / plugin_tool_surface_bytes (bytes of plugin tools inside the provider tools field + bytes of the plugin lines inside the system-prompt tool directory)
budget.measurement_rule: bytes and counts are measured, never estimated as tokens; no token figure is claimed anywhere in this package (no tokenizer and no paid provider call)

measured_result_as_of_segA.why_the_resident_target_is_missed: Preserving every legacy parameter costs bytes. An earlier draft met 70% only because it silently dropped 408 parameters across 38 tools (evidence/param-compatibility-segA.json); closing additionalProperties:false over that draft would have REJECTED those calls. Correctness was chosen over the byte budget, and the miss is reported rather than papered over.
measured_result_as_of_segA.what_reaches_the_target: The route-based presentation (Tool Search directory/code mode) is the lever that meets 70%: REN-03 measured 84.09% for this same plugin on that route. That reduction is orthogonal to schema convergence and is NOT re-measured here; the combined figure is a full-regression item and is not claimed.

sunset_gate.requirement: a legacy alias may be retired only when call telemetry shows zero use over the observation window
sunset_gate.reason: no call telemetry channel exists in the isolated harness, and no production traffic was observed. All 69 legacy names therefore stay resolvable through the adapter; none is deleted or disabled here.
sunset_gate.rollback: the original registration snapshot is preserved (see rollback.md), so any legacy name can be restored by route without touching data

operations.mutex_note: Deliberately EMPTY. A [reference_id, asset_id] mutual exclusion was drafted and then removed: the real declaration of video_project_update_asset_ref carries BOTH reference_id and asset_id (evidence/tool-surface-L1-baseline.json), so excluding them would falsely reject a legal update_ref call. Source-level evidence for a constraint like this is required before it is emitted, because an unenforced or over-broad annotation is worse than none.

operations.description: Run a media generation provider. Without mode=execute this only builds the plan; executing additionally requires accept_credit_spend=true. Providers: dreamina CLI (video, image, upscale), Doubao audio, KIE Suno. Direct or canvas target.
operations.search_keywords: generate generation create render produce video image upscale audio music voice doubao kie suno dreamina seedance cost credit provider plan execute

media_kind.desc: what is generated (valid combinations per provider). Named media_kind rather than kind because the legacy audio/music tools already declare `kind` meaning the ingested asset kind (raw/working); reusing the name would have collapsed two different meanings into one field

mode.desc: plan builds the request only; execute runs it and requires accept_credit_spend=true

target.desc: direct request, or canvas-slot driven (replaces the separate video_canvas_* wrappers)

slot_shape_id.desc: audio or video slot being filled (target=canvas)

accept_credit_spend.desc: consent to spend credits; required for mode=execute

run_preflight.desc: run a credit preflight before generating (defaults to true)

writeback_canvas.desc: write results back to the canvas

required_evidence.provider: registry-level selector: the provider enum selects which provider path runs; each path is backed by the service methods listed in `service` and asserted individually below
required_evidence.media_kind: registry-level selector: together with provider it selects the provider path; the valid (provider,media_kind) pairs are enumerated in `combinations` so an unsupported pair is rejected explicitly instead of silently dispatching. Renamed from kind to avoid colliding with the legacy kind field (ingested asset kind: raw/working)
required_evidence.mode: registry-level selector: plan builds the request only, execute is the cost-bearing path. The plan/generate verb split that would let a plan tool alias onto a generate tool is deliberately removed
required_evidence.accept_credit_spend (mode=execute): service.js:1805 (video), service.js:1979 (image), service.js:2142 (upscale) each throw unless accept_credit_spend === true
required_evidence.canvas_id (target=canvas): service.js:1700 canvasDreaminaCliGenerateVideo resolves the handoff from canvas_id and reports 'canvas generation handoff is not ready' when it cannot

combinations.note: The explicitly supported (provider, kind, mode, target) tuples, and the ones that are NOT supported. Every supported tuple resolves to exactly one legacy tool. Unsupported tuples are declared here and REJECTED by the adapter rather than silently dispatching somewhere unexpected - so no capability is invented and none is silently substituted.

unsupported.reason: the baseline has no direct dreamina CLI tool: all four dreamina tools are canvas-driven
the baseline has no image plan tool (planning exists for video only), so a plan-only image request is a NEW capability and is therefore not claimed
the baseline has no upscale plan tool; not claimed

operations.description: Migration-window compatibility entry: call one of the 69 original tool names through the reduced surface. The nested rgs are validated against that legacy tool's own per-mode sub-schema, so a value set that is legal for the wide union but illegal for the chosen branch is refused here.
operations.note: Compatibility entry, not a capability merge: legacy is deliberately EMPTY so it does not inflate the migration matrix or the merged-capability count. It exists so the previous tool names stay callable from the new package during the migration window; remove when callers have migrated. The 69 names it accepts are declared as the legacy_tool input enum.

legacy_tool.desc: the original tool name to call

args.desc: the original tool's arguments, validated against that tool's own narrow sub-schema

required_evidence.legacy_tool: must be one of the 69 declared legacy names; the dispatcher refuses anything else
required_evidence.args: validated by the plugin's own validateToolInput against the per-mode sub-schema emitted in schemas.json#by_mode, so branch-illegal values are rejected at the real handler entry
